mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% may signal monetary tightening, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in over 50% of the 20-day windows after FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Combined growth in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, which may boost economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the correlation between the combined labor indicators and S&P 500 returns is below 0.1 over a 3-year period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion may indicate reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows during a late-cycle expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which may lead to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 50% of the 60-day windows following GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 units may indicate strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows after HOUST exceeds 1500, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate a robust economy despite tight monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the combined effect of FEDFUNDS and UNRATE fails to correlate positively with S&P 500 returns (correlation < 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) may lead to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows during monetary tightening, the hypothesis is rejected.
